#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# demo.sh — launch the AO Adapter Proving Ground (or record it).
#
#   ./demo.sh              # interactive deck + stage
#   ./demo.sh --record     # same, captured to evalrig.cast with asciinema
#   ./demo.sh --record out.cast
#
# Works whether or not you're already inside Zellij:
#   - outside Zellij  -> starts a new Zellij session with the layout.
#   - inside Zellij   -> opens the demo as a new TAB in your current session
#                        (nesting a new session is what Zellij refuses).
#
# The deck (left) is `ao evalrig`; the stage (right) is a shell the deck drives
# to run the real `go test` for each cell. Quit the deck with `q`.
set -euo pipefail

here="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
repo="$(cd "$here/../.." && pwd)"
backend="$repo/backend"

for bin in zellij go; do
    command -v "$bin" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "demo.sh: '$bin' not found in PATH" >&2; exit 1; }
done

echo "Building ao …"
( cd "$backend" && go build -o "$backend/bin/ao" ./cmd/ao )
ao_bin="$backend/bin/ao"

# A resolved layout with absolute paths. Panes inherit the Zellij *server*
# environment, not this script's, so a relative cwd or a PATH export here would
# not reach them — bake the absolute binary path and cwd into the layout.
layout="$here/.evalrig.local.kdl"
cat > "$layout" <<KDL
layout {
    cwd "$backend"
    pane split_direction="vertical" {
        pane name="deck" size="58%" command="$ao_bin" {
            args "evalrig"
        }
        pane name="stage" size="42%"
    }
}
KDL

record=0
cast="$here/evalrig.cast"
if [[ "${1:-}" == "--record" ]]; then
    record=1
    [[ -n "${2:-}" ]] && cast="$2"
fi

# Already inside Zellij: open a new tab rather than nesting a session.
if [[ -n "${ZELLIJ:-}" ]]; then
    if [[ "$record" == 1 ]]; then
        echo "Note: --record must run from OUTSIDE Zellij (asciinema needs to own the session)." >&2
        echo "Opening the demo in a new tab instead — record your terminal separately." >&2
    fi
    echo "Inside Zellij → opening the proving ground in a new tab (switch tabs to see it)."
    exec zellij action new-tab --layout "$layout" --name evalrig
fi

# Fresh terminal: start a new named session with the layout.
session="evalrig-$$"
if [[ "$record" == 1 ]]; then
    command -v asciinema >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "demo.sh: asciinema not found" >&2; exit 1; }
    echo "Recording to $cast …"
    exec asciinema rec --overwrite -c "zellij --session '$session' --layout '$layout'" "$cast"
fi
exec zellij --session "$session" --layout "$layout"

lines: # A resolved layout with absolute paths. Panes inherit the Zellij *server*
# environment, not this script's, so a relative cwd or a PATH export here would
-# not reach them — bake the absolute binary path and cwd into the layout.
+# not reach them — bake the absolute binary path and cwd into each pane. The
+# cwd MUST be per-pane: a new tab in an existing session inherits the session's
+# cwd, and a layout-level `cwd` does not override it (so the stage would land in
+# the repo root and `go test ./internal/...` would fail to find the module).

input.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# demo.sh — launch the AO Adapter Proving Ground: two panes side by side,
# deck (ao evalrig) on the left, stage (a shell the deck drives) on the right.
#
#   ./demo.sh
#
# Works inside or outside Zellij:
#   - inside Zellij  -> opens the demo as a new TAB (Zellij won't nest sessions).
#   - outside Zellij -> starts a new session.
#
# The two-pane layout is passed inline (no layout file is written). Each pane's
# cwd is the absolute backend dir so the stage runs `go test ./internal/...`
# regardless of where Zellij was started. Quit the deck with `q`.
#
# To record: run `vhs evalrig.tape` for a standalone GIF of the deck, or
# screen-record this two-pane session.
set -euo pipefail

here="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
repo="$(cd "$here/../.." && pwd)"
backend="$repo/backend"

for bin in zellij go; do
    command -v "$bin" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "demo.sh: '$bin' not found in PATH" >&2; exit 1; }
done

echo "Building ao …"
( cd "$backend" && go build -o "$backend/bin/ao" ./cmd/ao )
ao_bin="$backend/bin/ao"

layout="layout {
    pane split_direction=\"vertical\" {
        pane name=\"deck\" size=\"58%\" cwd=\"$backend\" command=\"$ao_bin\" {
            args \"evalrig\"
        }
        pane name=\"stage\" size=\"42%\" cwd=\"$backend\"
    }
}"

if [[ -n "${ZELLIJ:-}" ]]; then
    echo "Inside Zellij → opening the proving ground in a new tab (switch tabs to see it)."
    exec zellij action new-tab --layout-string "$layout" --name evalrig
fi

exec zellij --session "evalrig-$$" --layout-string "$layout"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# demo.sh — launch the AO Adapter Proving Ground (or record it).
#
#   ./demo.sh              # interactive deck + stage
#   ./demo.sh --record     # same, captured to evalrig.cast with asciinema
#   ./demo.sh --record out.cast
#
# Works whether or not you're already inside Zellij:
#   - outside Zellij  -> starts a new Zellij session with the layout.
#   - inside Zellij   -> opens the demo as a new TAB in your current session
#                        (nesting a new session is what Zellij refuses).
#
# The deck (left) is `ao evalrig`; the stage (right) is a shell the deck drives
# to run the real `go test` for each cell. Quit the deck with `q`.
set -euo pipefail

here="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
repo="$(cd "$here/../.." && pwd)"
backend="$repo/backend"

for bin in zellij go; do
    command -v "$bin" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "demo.sh: '$bin' not found in PATH" >&2; exit 1; }
done

echo "Building ao …"
( cd "$backend" && go build -o "$backend/bin/ao" ./cmd/ao )
ao_bin="$backend/bin/ao"

# A resolved layout with absolute paths. Panes inherit the Zellij *server*
# environment, not this script's, so a relative cwd or a PATH export here would
# not reach them — bake the absolute binary path and cwd into each pane. The
# cwd MUST be per-pane: a new tab in an existing session inherits the session's
# cwd, and a layout-level `cwd` does not override it (so the stage would land in
# the repo root and `go test ./internal/...` would fail to find the module).
layout="$here/.evalrig.local.kdl"
cat > "$layout" <<KDL
layout {
    pane split_direction="vertical" {
        pane name="deck" size="58%" cwd="$backend" command="$ao_bin" {
            args "evalrig"
        }
        pane name="stage" size="42%" cwd="$backend"
    }
}
KDL

record=0
cast="$here/evalrig.cast"
if [[ "${1:-}" == "--record" ]]; then
    record=1
    [[ -n "${2:-}" ]] && cast="$2"
fi

# Already inside Zellij: open a new tab rather than nesting a session.
if [[ -n "${ZELLIJ:-}" ]]; then
    if [[ "$record" == 1 ]]; then
        echo "Note: --record must run from OUTSIDE Zellij (asciinema needs to own the session)." >&2
        echo "Opening the demo in a new tab instead — record your terminal separately." >&2
    fi
    echo "Inside Zellij → opening the proving ground in a new tab (switch tabs to see it)."
    exec zellij action new-tab --layout "$layout" --name evalrig
fi

# Fresh terminal: start a new named session with the layout.
session="evalrig-$$"
if [[ "$record" == 1 ]]; then
    command -v asciinema >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "demo.sh: asciinema not found" >&2; exit 1; }
    echo "Recording to $cast …"
    exec asciinema rec --overwrite -c "zellij --session '$session' --layout '$layout'" "$cast"
fi
exec zellij --session "$session" --layout "$layout"

# AO Adapter Proving Ground

An interactive, recordable demonstration that every agent adapter is tested
along the six dimensions we verify by hand:

| # | Dimension | What it proves |
|---|-----------|----------------|
| 1 | **spawn** | the launch command is well-formed, deterministic, and matches the declared prompt-delivery strategy |
| 2 | **activity** | the hooks the adapter installs are actually dispatched (`ao hooks <tok>` has a deriver) |
| 3 | **sessioninfo** | title/summary/id are derived from metadata only — never by reading transcripts |
| 4 | **permissions** | `default` emits no flag; each non-default mode maps to a distinct, real flag |
| 5 | **hooks** | install is idempotent and writes a worktree-local (non-tracked) config |
| 6 | **commands** | the exact launch/restore argv, snapshotted for review against each agent's CLI docs |

The verdicts come from the in-process conformance engine in
`backend/internal/adapters/agent/conformance` — the *same code CI runs* — so the
demo and the regression guard can never disagree.

## The two surfaces

- **Control deck** (`ao evalrig`) — a Bubble Tea TUI rendering the
  adapters × dimensions matrix. The presenter runs cells one keypress at a time.
- **Stage** — a sibling Zellij pane the deck drives (via `zellij action paste`)
  to run the real `go test` for each selected cell, so an audience watches
  genuine PASS lines while the matrix cell fills in.

```
┌─ deck (ao evalrig) ───────────┬─ stage (go test live) ─────────┐
│ HARNESS     SPAWN ACT INFO …  │ $ go test … -run …/spawn -v    │
│ claude-code   ✓    ✓   ✓  …   │ === RUN   TestConformance/…     │
│▸opencode      ✓    ▲   ✓  …   │ --- PASS: …                     │
│ …                             │                                 │
└───────────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────────┘
```

Legend: `✓` pass · `▲` gap (wired-but-broken) · `✗` fail (contract violation) ·
`–` n/a (adapter limitation) · `·` not run yet.

## Run it

```bash
# Interactive two-pane demo (Zellij). Requires: zellij, go.
test/evalrig/demo.sh
```

`demo.sh` works whether or not you're already inside Zellij: from a fresh
terminal it starts a new session; from inside an existing session it opens the
demo as a new **tab** (Zellij refuses to nest a new session). Either way it
generates a layout with absolute paths so the panes find `ao` and run `go test`
from `backend/` regardless of the inherited environment.

Keys: `enter` run+advance · `space`/`r` re-run · `a` run row · `A` run all ·
arrows / `hjkl` move · `q` quit.

Run the deck alone (matrix-only, no stage) from anywhere:

```bash
cd backend && go run ./cmd/ao evalrig
```

### Live mode (hybrid)

With a running daemon and a registered project, the deck can spawn a real agent
and watch its actual activity and session info:

```bash
ao start                                  # daemon
ao project add … && ao evalrig --project <project-id>
```

Press `L` on an adapter whose binary is installed: the deck spawns it via the
daemon and a live panel shows the real activity state
(`active → idle → waiting_input → exited`) and the hook-derived title as they
change. `x` stops watching. Adapters whose binary isn't installed stay
deterministic-only — the deck says so rather than failing.

## Record it

```bash
# Live, presenter-paced capture (terminal-native .cast). Requires: asciinema.
test/evalrig/demo.sh --record            # -> test/evalrig/evalrig.cast
asciinema play test/evalrig/evalrig.cast

# Deterministic, embeddable GIF trailer (matrix-only). Requires: vhs.
cd test/evalrig && vhs evalrig.tape      # -> evalrig.gif
```

Use **asciinema** to prove you drove it live at your own pace; use **VHS** to
regenerate a clean GIF for a README/Slack/PR. Both reuse the same deck — they're
recorders, not separate rigs.

## The engine underneath (run without the TUI)

```bash
cd backend

# The full matrix + per-cell detail, as text (report-only):
go test ./internal/adapters/agent/conformance/ -run TestConformance -v

# One cell:
go test ./internal/adapters/agent/conformance/ -run 'TestConformance/opencode/activity' -v

# Turn it into an enforcing CI gate (fail on FAIL/GAP and golden drift):
AOEVAL_STRICT=1 go test ./internal/adapters/agent/conformance/...

# Regenerate the golden command snapshots + matrix.txt after an intended change:
AOEVAL_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test ./internal/adapters/agent/conformance/...
```

Golden launch/restore commands live in
`backend/internal/adapters/agent/conformance/testdata/golden/<harness>.txt`.

## Adding a new adapter

A new harness is registered in one place —
`backend/internal/adapters/agent/registry` (`Constructors`) — and, if it reports
activity, mapped in `backend/internal/adapters/agent/activitydispatch`
(`Derivers`). The proving ground picks it up automatically; the conformance
suite will immediately show its row.

content.text:
You were right to push back — I'd been validating a single manual paste, not the keys you actually press. This time I reproduced it against the **real `ao evalrig` TUI** and verified the fix the same way.

## The bug (reproduced)

Pressing **`a`/`A`** fires every cell's check in its own goroutine; each typed `paste`+`Enter` into the stage, and they **interleaved** → `…-count=1go test…` → `invalid value "1go"`. I confirmed it by sending `a` to the real deck pane and seeing all six commands mashed on one line.

## The fix (verified against the real TUI)

1. **Serialized stage writes** — a mutex makes each `paste`+`Enter` atomic, so even rapid presses can't interleave.
2. **Only single-cell runs touch the stage** — `enter`/`space`/`r` show one test; `a`/`A` just fill the matrix in-process (no flood, no garble).

Then I drove the actual deck headlessly and checked the real stage:
- `a` (run row) → stage stays clean, **0** garbled lines
- single `enter` → exactly **1** clean command → `--- PASS: TestConformance/claude-code/spawn … ok …conformance`
- **3 rapid enters** → still **0** garbling

Plus a `-race` regression test (`TestStageSerializesConcurrentWrites`: 16 concurrent `Run`s produce perfectly paired paste→Enter, never two pastes in a row). Full build + lint + `-race` green.

## What you'll see now

```bash
test/evalrig/demo.sh
```

- **`enter`** on a cell → one real `go test … PASS` scrolls in the stage, cell flips.
- **`a` / `A`** → the matrix fills fast (verdicts are in-process); the stage isn't touched.

#
# demo.sh — launch the AO Adapter Proving Ground: two panes side by side,
# deck (ao evalrig) on the left, stage (a shell the deck drives) on the right.
#

}"

1	// Package evalrig is the interactive control deck of the AO Adapter Proving
2	// Ground: a Bubble Tea TUI that renders the adapters × six-dimensions eval
3	// matrix and lets a presenter run cells one keypress at a time, driving a
4	// sibling Zellij "stage" pane to show each check executing live. The verdicts
5	// come from the same in-process conformance engine CI runs, so the demo and the
6	// regression guard can never disagree.
7	package evalrig
8	
9	import (
10		"context"
11		"fmt"
12		"strings"
13	
14		tea "github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea"
15	
16		"github.com/aoagents/agent-orchestrator/backend/internal/evalrig/conformance"
17		"github.com/aoagents/agent-orchestrator/backend/internal/evalrig/registry"
18	)
19	
20	type cellState int
21	
22	const (
23		cellPending cellState = iota
24		cellRunning
25		cellDone
26	)
27	
28	// Model is the control-deck state.
29	type Model struct {
30		harnessed   []registry.HarnessAgent
31		dims        []string
32		state       map[string]map[string]cellState
33		result      map[string]map[string]conformance.Result
34		row, col    int
35		logs        []string
36		stage       *Stage
37		live        LiveConfig
38		liveSession *liveSession
39		liveCap     map[string]bool
40		width       int
41		quitting    bool
42	}
43	
44	// cellResultMsg carries a finished cell verdict back into Update.
45	type cellResultMsg struct {
46		harness string
47		dim     string
48		result  conformance.Result
49	}
50	
51	// New builds the deck over the registered adapters, a (possibly no-op) stage,
52	// and a (possibly disabled) live config.
53	func New(stage *Stage, live LiveConfig) Model {
54		harnessed := registry.Harnessed()
55		state := make(map[string]map[string]cellState, len(harnessed))
56		result := make(map[string]map[string]conformance.Result, len(harnessed))
57		for _, ha := range harnessed {
58			h := string(ha.Harness)
59			state[h] = map[string]cellState{}
60			result[h] = map[string]conformance.Result{}
61			for _, d := range conformance.Dimensions {
62				state[h][d] = cellPending
63			}
64		}
65		return Model{
66			harnessed: harnessed,
67			dims:      conformance.Dimensions,
68			state:     state,
69			result:    result,
70			stage:     stage,
71			live:      live,
72			liveCap:   map[string]bool{},
73		}
74	}
75	
76	// Init implements tea.Model.
77	func (m Model) Init() tea.Cmd { return nil }
78	
79	// Update implements tea.Model.
80	func (m Model) Update(msg tea.Msg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
81		switch msg := msg.(type) {
82		case tea.WindowSizeMsg:
83			m.width = msg.Width
84			return m, nil
85	
86		case cellResultMsg:
87			m.state[msg.harness][msg.dim] = cellDone
88			m.result[msg.harness][msg.dim] = msg.result
89			m.appendLog(fmt.Sprintf("%s/%s → %s", msg.harness, msg.dim, strings.ToUpper(string(msg.result.Status))))
90			return m, nil
91	
92		case liveSpawnResultMsg:
93			cmd := m.applyLiveSpawn(msg)
94			return m, cmd
95	
96		case livePollResultMsg:
97			cmd := m.applyLivePoll(msg)
98			return m, cmd
99	
100		case livePollTickMsg:
101			if m.liveSession != nil && m.liveSession.id == msg.id && !m.liveSession.terminated {
102				cmd := m.pollCmd(msg.id)
103				return m, cmd
104			}
105			return m, nil
106	
107		case tea.KeyMsg:
108			return m.handleKey(msg)
109		}
110		return m, nil
111	}
112	
113	func (m Model) handleKey(msg tea.KeyMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
114		switch msg.String() {
115		case "q", "ctrl+c", "esc":
116			m.quitting = true
117			return m, tea.Quit
118		case "up", "k":
119			m.row = clamp(m.row-1, len(m.harnessed)-1)
120		case "down", "j":
121			m.row = clamp(m.row+1, len(m.harnessed)-1)
122		case "left", "h":
123			m.col = clamp(m.col-1, len(m.dims)-1)
124		case "right", "l":
125			m.col = clamp(m.col+1, len(m.dims)-1)
126		case "enter":
127			// Run the selected cell, then advance to the next — the "keep pressing
128			// enter to run the next test" presenter flow.
129			cmd := m.runSelected()
130			m.advance()
131			return m, cmd
132		case " ", "r":
133			// Re-run the selected cell in place (no cursor advance).
134			cmd := m.runSelected()
135			return m, cmd
136		case "a":
137			// Run every dimension for the current adapter.
138			cmd := m.runRow(m.row)
139			return m, cmd
140		case "A":
141			// Run the whole matrix.
142			cmd := m.runAll()
143			return m, cmd
144		case "L":
145			// Live-spawn the selected adapter (if a daemon + project are configured).
146			cmd := m.startLive()
147			return m, cmd
148		case "x":
149			// Stop watching the current live session.
150			if m.liveSession != nil {
151				m.appendLog(fmt.Sprintf("live: stopped watching %s", m.liveSession.id))
152				m.liveSession = nil
153			}
154		}
155		return m, nil
156	}
157	
158	func (m *Model) runSelected() tea.Cmd {
159		// A deliberate single-cell run drives the stage so the audience watches the
160		// real test execute.
161		return m.runCell(m.row, m.col, true)
162	}
163	
164	// runCell runs one (adapter, dimension) check in-process. When showStage is
165	// true it also types the matching `go test` into the stage pane. Bulk runs pass
166	// false: typing dozens of commands into one shell would both flood it and — even
167	// serialized — queue behind each other, so they only update the matrix.
168	func (m *Model) runCell(row, col int, showStage bool) tea.Cmd {
169		ha := m.harnessed[row]
170		h := string(ha.Harness)
171		dim := m.dims[col]
172		if m.state[h][dim] == cellRunning {
173			return nil
174		}
175		m.state[h][dim] = cellRunning
176		m.appendLog(fmt.Sprintf("running %s/%s …", h, dim))
177		stage := m.stage
178		return func() tea.Msg {
179			ctx := context.Background()
180			if showStage {
181				_ = stage.Run(ctx, goTestCommand(h, dim))
182			}
183			res, _ := conformance.RunDimension(ctx, ha, dim)
184			return cellResultMsg{harness: h, dim: dim, result: res}
185		}
186	}
187	
188	func (m *Model) runRow(row int) tea.Cmd {
189		cmds := make([]tea.Cmd, 0, len(m.dims))
190		for c := range m.dims {
191			if cmd := m.runCell(row, c, false); cmd != nil {
192				cmds = append(cmds, cmd)
193			}
194		}
195		return tea.Batch(cmds...)
196	}
197	
198	func (m *Model) runAll() tea.Cmd {
199		cmds := make([]tea.Cmd, 0, len(m.harnessed)*len(m.dims))
200		for r := range m.harnessed {
201			for c := range m.dims {
202				if cmd := m.runCell(r, c, false); cmd != nil {
203					cmds = append(cmds, cmd)
204				}
205			}
206		}
207		return tea.Batch(cmds...)
208	}
209	
210	// advance moves the cursor to the next cell, left-to-right then down a row.
211	func (m *Model) advance() {
212		m.col++
213		if m.col >= len(m.dims) {
214			m.col = 0
215			if m.row < len(m.harnessed)-1 {
216				m.row++
217			} else {
218				m.col = len(m.dims) - 1 // stay on the last cell
219			}
220		}
221	}
222	
223	func (m *Model) appendLog(line string) {
224		m.logs = append(m.logs, line)
225		if len(m.logs) > 6 {
226			m.logs = m.logs[len(m.logs)-6:]
227		}
228	}
229	
230	// goTestCommand is the command the stage runs to demonstrate one cell: the real
231	// conformance subtest, in verbose mode, so the audience sees genuine PASS lines.
232	func goTestCommand(harness, dim string) string {
233		return fmt.Sprintf(
234			"go test ./internal/evalrig/conformance/ -run 'TestConformance/%s/%s' -v -count=1",
235			harness, dim,
236		)
237	}
238	
239	// clamp bounds v to [0, hi]; the cursor never goes below the first row/column.
240	func clamp(v, hi int) int {
241		if v < 0 {
242			return 0
243		}
244		if v > hi {
245			return hi
246		}
247		return v
248	}
